summary: Feed c078_crc_link to APM is degraded: VF-1 port 1 ingress has high CRC/alignment errors (0.165%) and 1.24% packet loss on the link from DC-CORE-1 Gi1/0/48 SPAN destination. Both faults corrupt/lose traffic before the APM, breaking transaction visibility.

findings.root_cause: VF-1 port 1 (input) received 6,720 damaged frames with CRC/alignment errors (0.165% vs 0.001% threshold). Classic Layer-1 fault on the ingress link into the packet broker - faulty/dirty cable or optic, or duplex mismatch corrupting frames in transit.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM receives corrupted frames that are dropped by NIC/broker ASIC; results in incomplete TCP reassembly, gaps in transaction traces, false retransmission/latency signals and reduced application performance coverage.

recommended_fix.why: Clean Layer-1 is prerequisite for APM accuracy - damaged frames cannot be analyzed and are discarded, so fixing cable/optic/duplex restores complete, correct traffic to the tool.

findings.root_cause: 1.24% loss on the wire between DC-CORE-1 Gi1/0/48 (SPAN destination) and VF-1 port 1 (input): 4,125,000 packets sent but only 4,073,940 received (~51,060 packets lost). Loss occurs before the visibility fabric due to faulty cable/optic, intermediate device, or SPAN oversubscription on that link.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM loses ~1 in 80 packets before analysis, causing broken flows, missed requests/responses, inaccurate response-time and availability calculations, and blind spots for intermittent application issues.

recommended_fix.why: APM needs lossless delivery for transaction reconstruction; repairing/replacing the inter-switch link and verifying SPAN destination capacity ensures the APM sees the full packet stream.
